title: How rhyme and rhythm make a poem sing
examples: What is rhythm in a poem?
How do I find words that rhyme?

explain.say: Say this with me. Twinkle, twinkle, little star, how I wonder what you are. Star and are end with the same sound. Poems use rhyme and rhythm. Look at the board. This rhyme family is cat, hat, mat and bat. They all end with the sound at.

draw.text: How rhyme and rhythm make a poem sing

explain.say: Words that end with the same sound rhyme. Look at the second family: night, light, kite and bright. Kite has a different spelling. It still rhymes, because rhyme is about sound. Add one more word to this family.
Rhythm is the beat of a poem. Look at the board: but, ter, fly. Clap it with me. Some beats are strong. Some beats are soft. In butterfly, the first beat is strong.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: BUT-ter-fly: one strong beat, two soft

explain.say: Poems often repeat strong and soft beats. Look at the line on the board. It goes up for a strong beat and down for a soft beat. Say twinkle, twinkle, little star. Tap your hand on each strong beat.
Look at the last rhyme family: cake, lake, snake and shake. Rhyme and rhythm make poems easy to remember. Can you say another word that rhymes with cake?

faq.a: Rhyme is when words end with the same sound, like cat and hat, or night and kite.

faq.q: What is rhythm in a poem?
faq.a: Rhythm is the beat of a poem: the pattern of strong and soft syllables, like a drum beat under the words.

faq.q: How do I find words that rhyme?
faq.a: Take the end sound of a word, like ake, then go through the alphabet: bake, cake, lake, make, snake, take.

faq.q: Do rhyming words have to be spelled the same?
faq.a: No. Rhyme is about sound. Kite and night rhyme, and so do blue and through.
No. Many poems, called free verse, do not rhyme at all. They use rhythm, pictures and feelings instead.

facts: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star was written by Jane Taylor and published in 1806.
Rhyme and rhythm help memory, which is why ancient stories were often told in verse.
